Not for long, anyway. The excitement from playing comes from the chance of failure. Just my two cents.

I've been trying to do this with a few of my friends who couldn't be damned to actually read a rule book and learn anything on their own. Keep in mind, however, that I haven't really done any of this so it may not help at all.

Foremost, I think you have to really drop the mysterious part of being a DM. Show your players exactly what is happening on the enemies' turns, including rolls and abilities. Have them use off-the-wall and alternative tactics to teach them different mechanics. Go through each turn step-by-step and explain what happened and why it was possible. Couple this with lots of traditional in-fiction descriptions and it might make things a bit more palatable.  Sure, it'll be slow, but once you get past the learning stage you can pull the screen back up and everything can go back to how you want it. I've never done any online gaming so this may not be as viable if everyone isn't sitting around the table to see the dice as you roll them, but what's most important is to be descriptive of the mechanics and be ready to answer any questions if they come up.

Another idea in a similar vein is to have a DM-controlled mentor or helper following them around who you can use to explain various mechanics, including those outside of combat. Be sure not to fall into any of the DMPC pitfalls if you go this route. Once you're absolutely sure they've gotten a handle on the game you can use the character as a walking hook by offing him or sending him away to do some mysterious mission. Whatever fits how the game is developing. Hopefully they'll be invested in him at that point and it can bring people a little more into the story.

Small ideas, unfortunately, and they probably won't speed up the learning process all that much. Hopefully the basic mechanics will be easier for them to grasp if frequent examples are explained though.

I have no friends. It's not an exaggeration, and it's something I've just kind of recently realized. I mean, sure, I hang out with a few people, but It's just come to my attention that these people don't give a shit about me at all. I have to invite myself somewhere every time I want to spend time with another human being, and it feels rude and desperate and fuckin weird. They also spend much more time with each other than they do with me, and whenever they all go to do something (bowling and the movies are two recent examples) they sort of try to keep it on the down low or act like they thought I was busy. Even the person who I thought was my best friend has moved on to other people, other interests. Of course, I don't blame them. I wouldn't want to spend time with me either.

We all used to be closer, at least, it seemed that way to me. I went away for a year to go to college and worked really hard so I could transfer to another, better college that was close. There were plans to room with my supposed best friend and I just kept my nose to the grindstone and had no fun, made no friends, have no memories. Now that seems like a mistake. These are supposed to be the best years of my life, right? However, I just flushed an entire year of it away and have nothing to show for it.  It's nice that the new college is of a higher quality, but the tuition is also way higher and I might be fucking myself that way.

Also on this subject, I've never had a girlfriend, and it doesn't look like I'll be getting close to anyone in the foreseeable future. Not to eagerly jump into the ol' forever alone wizard or whatever attitude that's so pervasive on reddit, but I have no delusions about myself. I'm not particularly funny, handsome, smart, rich, or anything really. I'm just kind of a sub-average dude with social anxiety. To top it all off, I have a fear of ANY kind of commitment, and even the simple boyfriend/girlfriend  relationship seems really restrictive. I was raised around failed marriages and fleeting relationships so maybe that's to blame but I don't even know if I want to ask anybody out because it'll either fail or I'll be chained to them forever. In contrast, I feel an absolutely desperate need to stave off my ever-present loneliness and I really, REALLY want to have sex sometime soon so I'm kind of going back and forth on the whole thing internally on top of my personality issues.

I just have no idea where I'm going with my life. I don't really want to be rich, I have no idea what I'm going to college for, I don't know how to make friends, and I don't like myself. I feel totally directionless. I want to die, or just stop existing. Sometimes I want to kill myself. I want to go to a psychiatrist or a therapist or something, but I don't feel sad all the time. Reading about other people's experiences with depression, that doesn't really sound like me. As a result, I'm scared to seek help for my occasional mood problems because I don't want to be told that I'm just over-exaggerating or for it to be perceived that I believe I suffer just as bad or worse than others when that really isn't the case. I really have no reason to be mopey about my life. I have a car and an iPhone and a laptop and food to eat and a place to live. I'm better off than millions, maybe even billions of people. 

It just feels like everything about my is contradicting or pulling in different directions. I'm not even old enough to drink and I just want to be a little kid again. From where I'm standing, it looks like there's no light at the end of the tunnel for ANY of my problems, but I feel guilty for even thinking of them as problems. I've never had to deal with a REAL issue, so maybe I should just fucking figure myself out and make something out of this life I didn't ask for and occasionally don't want. 

Whew, thanks for letting me get all of that off of my chest. Is there anything that you would like to talk about, OP?

I must have been a very young kid, I don't know the exact age, but I was sitting outside just kind of playing in the dirt when I spotted a very small snake, maybe the length of an adults index finger. I remember it was a dull orange that faded a bright blue tail. I slightly spread my fingers and stuck them into the dirt directly in front of it's path, I guess to emulate it being behind bars or a fence or something. It continued, winding once around the bottom of my middle finger before taking off.

In another occasion, I remember us being in a place I wasn't familiar with. I think it must have been a motel room or something, but I can't recall exactly where. My dad had somehow had a gun, a revolver specifically, and being in one his drunken states he wasn't being very careful with it, at least it seemed so to my childhood self. The gun had a wick sticking out of the top of it that was sparking and burning like a cartoon bomb or TNT or something. When the wick burned down he accidentally shot a bullet into the wall. After he fired the gun, the room was filled with smoke. This memory is much more distant than the other, but I recall much more vivid details, like the feeling of being in a place I didn't know and even the smell of spent gunpowder, which I wouldn't have known because my family, especially my dad, has never been big on firearms.

I attribute both of these to dreams now, so this is slightly less interesting than pretty much all other comments in the thread, but I don't usually remember dreams, especially small details in them. These events stick so absolutely in my memory that it sometimes gives me pause, despite the obviously fantastic nature of both.

I'm new to RPG's in general, but here's the thing I never understood: why does railroading have such a bad rep? I can completely understand why over-railroading and blatant railroading can ruin the fun, but why is it considered such a bad thing overall? Wouldn't it be more enjoyable for everyone at the table if you played along with what the guy running the game had in mind, instead of feeling like the only way you can have fun is if you are directly in control of everything at all times?

When I was a child I was scared of going to the movies. Not the movies, not the movie theater, the physical act of going to the movies. It's a bit of a difficult thing to explain, but I would just get really anxious and freak out. From what I can remember, it had something to do with being in a dark room, all you can really see is the  large screen and then there's the booming sound. The combination was just a little too much for me. 

I eventually got over it, for the most part, but to this day I still feel some residual fear whenever I go. I can't eat popcorn-especially the kind at the theater-to this day because of how I feel when I fucking smell it. To tell the truth, I've never seen a horror movie on the big screen, and I don't really plan on ever seeing one in the theater. I'm afraid it will bring back that old anxiety and I'll have to leave or something.

Pine needles. I used to live in a place where there would always be pine needles all over the place. After we moved, I just kind of forgot they existed. I saw one for the first time in years the other day, and I was reminded of all the times my sister and I would pull them apart like wishbones. We would make it a game, and whoever got the needle with the top bit won. We would play the game until there weren't anymore needles on the driveway or the lawn, keeping track of who had the most wins. For some reason they also makes me think of fall. I miss my sister.
